OPERATION NEEDLE AND FANG - DEVELOPMENT DUEL
Syria / 08:00 local / one player OH-58D versus one AI Mi-24V

OBJECTIVE
Destroy BOTH the enemy Hind and its defended DShK technical. Protect your own DShK technical. Loss of your aircraft or defended vehicle means immediate failure; merely destroying one enemy does not win. Friendly losses take precedence if both sides are destroyed in the same evaluation interval. Victory is assessed on destruction, without a required recovery. Flying continues after the result.

START / LOADOUT
You are Anvil 1-1, NEEDLE, hot on a visible single helipad at BLUE FARP. FANG starts hot on its own RED FARP. Both use fixed zero-AGL ground starts; no stacked parking allocations. Two Stingers and an M3P .50-cal gun with 500 rounds, 30 flares, 181.4 kg fuel (about 400 lb). Use Stingers against the Hind and the gun against the unarmored enemy technical. There are no Hellfires, wingmen, jets or additional combat units. The technical can shoot back; avoid a prolonged stationary hover in its sight line. Check actual gross weight, hover capability and fuel reserve in the cockpit. Pad warehouses are configured, but ground-service capability is not claimed without service vehicles/native acceptance.

GEOGRAPHY / INTELLIGENCE
The defended vehicles are 8.0 nm apart, roughly five to six minutes at 90 kt before searching or combat. FARPs are near their own objectives; allow about 15-25 minutes for the duel, without a mission deadline. Both vehicles remain at their briefing-time positions beside authored outbuildings; terrain/forest concealment and landing fit require flight inspection. Your map shows friendly units only and labels are off. The exact RED OBJECTIVE marker and Kiowa target point 1T are fixed intelligence; the Hind's position is unknown. No live enemy tracking, scripted spotting or automatic aircraft coordinates are provided.

MMS PREPOINT
Select MMS PREPT, R2 PPT, enter 1T and press Enter. The stored record is 1T|1|UNK and identifies the defended technical, not the Hind. It is not a weapons lock. Cockpit import/alignment requires native verification. The enemy asset is not on your flight route: WP2 is an optional maneuver reference, WP3 is your home pad. No route forces you to fly over the technical.

ENEMY BEHAVIOR
The Hind's native launch is released after your first takeoff; waiting on the pad does not start its attack. It then hunts your defended vehicle and may engage your Kiowa if detected. Both sides know the fixed objective locations. Native sensing controls the air encounter: the script never feeds your live aircraft coordinates to the Hind. The Hind carries two S-8 rocket pods and its native gun, without ATGMs, High skill and 900 kg fuel. Launch, terrain masking, attack behavior and firing effectiveness need a DCS sortie; a launch request is not proof of takeoff. Ground objectives may defend themselves from mission start.

CONTROL / REPORTS
F10 Other > Duel > Status / objectives is the only mission command. Status reports your asset's condition and confirmed enemy losses, without giving Hind location or enemy group names. One-time reports announce engagement release, observed Hind takeoff and confirmed destroyed objectives. Loss of the Hind before it launches counts only after that unit has actually been acquired. Missing enemy units at initial loading never award a victory. Objective or mandatory AI task setup failure reports failure instead of a false success. No recovery smoke.

RADIOS / FIRST FLIGHT CHECK
Package 251.000 AM; BLUE FARP 128.500 AM. Requires Syria and OH-58D only; AI Mi-24V is a built-in asset. No external framework or hook is needed to play. Inspect both starts/pads, ground-unit/building fit and both FARP clearings, then observe the Hind's real departure and ability to attack your technical/engage your Kiowa. Verify Stinger acquisition, gun effectiveness, terrain and fuel. This first slice has not been flown; archive/mock checks do not establish a fair or playable native dogfight. Restart the mission after updates.
